title: Two stress cases fail on Windows: the query exceeds the command-line limit
goal: python _tools/stress_test.py exits 0 on Windows: the 10k-word and 120k-char search cases pass their query without exceeding the Windows command-line limit, and still test the same input size on macOS and Linux.
notes: Needs a Windows machine to confirm. A local Windows run (Windows 11, cp1250 locale, Python 3.14.7, uv 0.12.19, Git for Windows 2.55, 8 xdist workers) at 3ff06b7: stress_test.py gives 2 failed, 86 passed, 1 skipped in 452 s. test_stress.py::test_base[search 10k-word query] and ::test_base[search 120k-char single token] (test_stress.py:140-141) pass the query as one argument; test_stress.py:46 run -> FileNotFoundError [WinError 206]: a Windows command line holds at most 32,767 characters. rag.py is not at fault. Options: feed the query another way if rag.py search can take one (then widen touches to _tools/rag.py), or cap the size on win32 below the limit and say so in the case's comment, as the 120k case already notes Linux's 128 KiB argv cap.
